# agent

The turn loop: prompt, stream, run tools, steer, queue.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-agent.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-agent.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** [session](session.md), [provider](provider.md), [tools](tools.md)
- **Required by:** [cache-warm](cache-warm.md), [compaction](compaction.md), [cowboy](cowboy.md), [handoff](handoff.md), [merge](merge.md), [naming](naming.md), [recap](recap.md), [resilience](resilience.md), [retry](retry.md), [seed](seed.md), [supervisor](supervisor.md), [tasks](tasks.md), [tools-agent](tools-agent.md), [tools-events](tools-events.md), [tools-sessions](tools-sessions.md)

## About

One turn: the user's message goes in, the model streams text and
thinking, asks for tools, the harness runs them (through the
permission chain) and feeds the results back, until the model stops.
Providers that run their own loop (hosted) hand each tool call to us
through a `:respond` callback; native providers stop with `tool-use`
and are called again with the results.  Steering messages sent while
a turn runs are delivered once, at the next step boundary: with the
next tool result, or as the next user message when the model stops
first.  Until then the user can take one back (`agent/withdraw`).
Queued messages wait for the turn to end and then go out
together as a turn of their own.  A message is delivered when it
starts a turn or steers one, a queued one when its queue goes out;
then, and only then, the `agent/message` filters see it and may
change it (task mode sends a task waiting for review back this way).
A model that stops on its own, with nothing steering, is not let go
at once: the `agent/stop` filters may answer it with a message of the
harness's and a step more, a few times at most (`harness-agent--stopped`).

A tool result may carry pictures for the model (`:images`, as read_file
on an image gives): a hosted loop is handed them with the result, a
native one reads them from the transcript with its next request, and
only a model that reads images is sent any (see "Images tools return").
The images a steering message attached go the same way: a hosted loop
gets them with the tool result that carries the message's text, each
after its token ([image 1]), and a native one with the message itself
in its next request (see `harness-agent--with-steering`).

A provider may run a tool of its own in place of a harness tool (see
`tools/builtin`): Claude Code's web search for web_search, say.  It
reports such a call (a `tool-call` event marked `:builtin`), asks the
harness whether it may run (`tool-permission`, decided by
`tools/authorize`) and reports its result (`tool-result`).  The turn
records them as it records the calls it runs, and gives every such
call still open a result once the provider is done, since a call
without a result breaks the transcript for providers that pair them.

The loop is entirely event driven: nothing here waits.

## Provides

### Methods

- `agent/activity` (session-id) — Return what SESSION-ID's running turn is doing now, or nil.
- `agent/cancel` (session-id) — Cancel the running turn of SESSION-ID, if any.
- `agent/note-activity` (session-id activity) — Announce ACTIVITY as what SESSION-ID's turn does, before the turn starts.
- `agent/outstanding` (session-id) — Return what runs for SESSION-ID outside its own turn, as a short text, or nil.
- `agent/prompt` (session-id blocks &optional opts) — Send BLOCKS (content blocks, or a string) to SESSION-ID.
- `agent/running` (&optional session-id) — Return running session ids, or non-nil when SESSION-ID is running.
- `agent/send-queue` (session-id &optional qids) — Send the queued messages of SESSION-ID as one turn; return its promise.
- `agent/stop-outstanding` (session-id &optional reason) — Stop what runs for SESSION-ID outside its own turn; return what it stopped.
- `agent/withdraw` (session-id node-id) — Take back the steering message NODE-ID of SESSION-ID; return the node it was.

### Events

- `agent/activity-changed` — (SESSION-ID ACTIVITY) when what a running turn does changes; ACTIVITY nil once it ends (see `agent/activity`)
- `agent/call-usage` — (SESSION-ID USAGE) when a model call of a hosted loop's turn reports its usage, (:output N), with `:context` N, the size of the call's prompt, when the provider knows it; the turn's `usage` event counts it
- `agent/cancelling` — (SESSION-ID) when the running turn is cancelled, before it ends: a gate holding the turn up lets it go
- `agent/quota` — (SESSION-ID WINDOWS)
- `agent/steered` — (SESSION-ID)
- `agent/step-started` — (SESSION-ID STEP)
- `agent/stream` — (SESSION-ID NODE-ID KIND DELTA)
- `agent/tool-call` — (SESSION-ID NODE)
- `agent/tool-result` — (SESSION-ID NODE)
- `agent/turn-ended` — (SESSION-ID REASON)
- `agent/turn-started` — (SESSION-ID)

### Filter chains it runs

- `agent/before-turn`
- `agent/message`
- `agent/outstanding`
- `agent/step`
- `agent/step-error`
- `agent/stop`
- `agent/stop-outstanding`
- `agent/system-prompt`
- `tools/output-text`

### Options

- `harness-agent-history-images` — How many of the newest images that tools returned a request carries.
